misconceptions.description: Assuming maximum bending moment occurs at the supports because reactions are large there
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports M_max at a support of a simply supported beam
misconceptions.feedback: M is extremized where V crosses zero (dM/dx = V). For a simply supported beam, M is zero at pin/roller supports and largest somewhere in the span.

misconceptions.description: Treating distributed load w(x) as if it equals shear V(x) rather than its slope
misconceptions.trigger: learner sets V(x) = w(x) when computing reactions or shear
misconceptions.feedback: The relationship is dV/dx = -w, not V = w. Distributed load w is the rate at which shear changes along the beam, not the shear itself.

misconceptions.description: Believing left-side and right-side analyses can yield different internal forces at the same cut
misconceptions.trigger: learner gets different M values from left and right and believes both are correct
misconceptions.feedback: Newton's third law guarantees equal-and-opposite force pairs on the two cut faces. With consistent sign convention applied to both, you get the same N, V, M. Disagreement means a sign-convention error.

misconceptions.description: Assuming the shear diagram remains continuous across a point load
misconceptions.trigger: learner draws V(x) as a smooth function passing through a point-load location
misconceptions.feedback: Point loads cause step discontinuities in V; point couples cause steps in M; only continuous distributed loading gives smooth diagrams.
